message: Warfarin and ibuprofen together significantly increase the risk of serious bleeding. Avoid ibuprofen while taking warfarin.
Combining warfarin with aspirin raises the risk of stomach bleeding and major bleeding events.
Metronidazole slows warfarin breakdown, sharply increasing bleeding risk.
Clarithromycin raises simvastatin levels and can cause muscle damage. Avoid the combination.
Itraconazole greatly increases simvastatin levels and the risk of muscle injury.
Ibuprofen reduces methotrexate clearance, which can cause serious bone-marrow and kidney toxicity.
Taking sildenafil with nitroglycerin or other nitrates can cause a life-threatening drop in blood pressure.
Omeprazole can reduce clopidogrel's ability to prevent blood clots. A different heartburn medicine may be better.
Ibuprofen can raise lithium levels to a toxic range, affecting kidneys and the nervous system.
Tramadol with sertraline may cause serotonin syndrome, a serious condition needing urgent care.
Amiodarone increases digoxin levels and the risk of dangerous heart rhythm side effects.
Cimetidine can increase metformin levels and the risk of lactic acidosis. Ask your doctor before combining.
Antacids reduce doxycycline absorption. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.
Combining lisinopril with spironolactone can cause dangerously high potassium in the blood.
Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels and adds to the risk of muscle damage. Limit the simvastatin dose.
Fluoxetine with tramadol increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures.
Antacids stop levofloxacin from being absorbed well. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.
Propranolol can block the relief salbutamol provides during an asthma attack. Use with caution.
